newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TO START TRANSPORT PRIVATISATION DEALS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TO START TRANSPORT PRIVATISATION DEALS.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim transport minister said on Tuesday priorities would be given to privatisation and concession deals in the transport sector.
Wilhelm Kraus said a new department, specialised in privatisation, would be set up in the ministry in an attempt to speed up the process and manage proceeds from privatisation deals.

"It is an anachronism to have a state-run cargo road transport. I think that municipalities can privatise their public transport and transport infrastructure including bus stations," Kraus told a news conference.

Kraus said the interim caretaker government, which will be in power until general elections on April 19, plans to start giving concessions for international road corridors passing through Bulgaria's territory.
"Bulgaria lies on a crossroad and four (international) corridors are crossing it but we will give a priority to the East-West road," he said.

The East-West highway, which will cost millions of dollars, is projected to link by road and railway southern Italian ports via Duras in Albania and Macedonia with Turkey and via the Bulgarian Black Sea ports of Bourgas and Varna with former Soviet republics.
"It is of an enormous importance to find investments and realise the project," Kraus said.
He said he was in favour of privatising the Balkan Airlines and giving concessions for developing airports and ports in the country.
A procedure for privatising the national carrier, which is plagued by losses, was started in 1992 but the privatisation agency suspended it in 1995, citing a lack of investors.
